9	
10	As of 2026-06-07 the noisy-label-robust node-classification project (Cora/CiteSeer, no heterophilous graphs) made a confirmed direction pivot, recorded in `02_experiment_history_and_lessons.md` §12 and `external/NoisyGL/runs/orgingb_noisygl_experiment_history_20260604.md` §9.
11	
12	Three evidence-backed conclusions:
13	1. **Graph-aware granular ball is dropped as a headline novelty** — on Cora/CiteSeer the topology increment `dcgb − dcgb_emb_only` is ±0.001 (purity/AUROC) across all 8 conditions; adjacency is redundant with features/GRACE on homophilous graphs.
14	2. **Reciprocal mutual-kNN reliable ball is the real positive signal** — ordinary GB purity collapses on raw features (Cora 0.30) while mutual-kNN balls recover it (0.78–0.84); AUROC over `gb` beats baseline with non-overlapping std in 4/4 settings.
15	3. **Supervised GCN representation is unreliable under label noise** — S1 (ReliableGB-GCN reweight) ties GCN (0.705, best_phase=warmup) because GCN val peaks ~epoch 6 then memorizes noise; this motivates building the same reliable balls on a label-free contrastive representation.
16	
17	Candidate paper mainline: **label-free contrastive representation + mutual-kNN reliable granular ball + conservative noise-aware training** (NOT graph-aware).
18	
19	Update 2026-06-10 (frozen-GRACE-ball + fresh end-to-end GCN line, NoisyGL percent split 0.2/0.1/0.7 uniform 0.4):
20	- **SoftDist is the confirmed best mechanism**: geometric balls on frozen GRACE H + multiclass-alpha ball-distribution soft targets + fresh GCN. 5-seed: Cora 0.795±0.009 (GCN+CE 0.784), CiteSeer 0.674±0.011 (GCN+CE 0.653); beats shuffled everywhere; loses to NRGNN (0.811/0.703) by ~1.5-3pp.
21	- **Failed add-ons (all seed0-refuted)**: dynamic alpha (self-reinforcing), ball-consistency regularizer, NRGNN+BallAux (ball signal redundant with graph propagation), and E1 label-aware adaptive granularity.
22	- **E1 negative result (2026-06-10)**: purity-coverage adaptive ball splitting (3 variants: threshold/strict-gain/multi-attempt-gain) cannot beat geometric balls at 20% coverage — per-ball noisy purity estimates (5-15 votes, noise ceiling ~0.66, std ~0.15) are too weak to drive granularity; CDR never dropped. Report: `external/NoisyGL/runs/adaptive_gb_seed0_rocm_20260610/adaptive_gb_e1_seed0_rocm_report_20260610.md`. E2 (unlabeled expansion on adaptive purity) cancelled with it.
23	- **Decided fallback: Route A** — paper positions SoftDist as first GB mechanism for noisy-label node classification + coverage sensitivity + mechanism-boundary negative results; do not chase NRGNN on its home regime.
24	
25	Update 2026-06-11 (XH mainline confirmed, 5-seed):
26	- **SoftDist [X||H] is the new mainline**: concat row-L2-normalized GRACE H onto GCN input features + SoftDist ball targets. 5-seed: Cora **0.8137±0.0067 (≥ NRGNN 0.8107±0.0230, 3× lower std)**, CiteSeer 0.6891±0.0159 (NRGNN 0.7027, gap -1.36pp). Full ablation chain clean: H-on-CE +1.9/+2.3pp, ball-on-H +1.1/+1.3pp, real>shuffled 5/5 both datasets. Cora seed0 (ball-on-H negative) was misleading.
27	- Phase 4a early-learning arbitration diagnostic FAILED its gates (Cora: too few protected; CiteSeer: protection precision 48-68% < 70%). X-only warmup recheck (4a-2) also failed identically → **Phase 4 permanently closed**; clean mechanism boundary: early-learning confidence (coupled or independent of H) cannot safely protect clean labels in this pipeline.
28	- **Noise grid regime analysis done (2026-06-11)**: no strict regime win vs NRGNN. Cora = tie in 4/5 regimes (competitive, lower variance); CiteSeer = loss everywhere; uniform 0.6 = big loss (offline correction breaks down, NRGNN online mechanism wins; Cora real even loses to shuffled there). Ball increment peaks at uniform 0.4 / pair 0.4; redundant at low noise. Report: `runs/noise_grid_rocm_20260611/`.
29	- **Mechanism exploration is CONCLUDED.** Final method = SoftDist [X||H]. Paper claims: (1) simple non-iterative GB pipeline competitive with NRGNN on Cora with 3× lower variance, (2) label-noise-immune representation stage (same H reused across all regimes), (3) clean attribution chain, (4) honest applicability boundary (CiteSeer, high uniform noise) + five mechanism-boundary negative results. Next work is paper writing, not more mechanisms.
30	
31	Update 2026-06-12 (literature mining closed): 13 GB+DL papers audited — 12 re-skins of closed directions or domain-mismatched; the survivor (MGNR multi-granularity consistency gate) failed preregistered gates (protection precision 0.52 < 0.70 — cross-scale disagreement marks vote ambiguity, not clean-label boundaries). **Three independent gate signals now refuted: vote-count, temporal, scale** — clean-vs-noisy is inseparable among ball-correction candidates at 20% coverage / 40% noise. Report: `runs/multigranularity_diag_20260612/`.
32	
33	Update 2026-06-12 (Phase 8-11 SSL upgrade / dataset / backbone — all four resolved):
34	- **Phase 8 probe**: CCA-SSG beat GRACE probe on both datasets (+2.7/+1.6pp clean); GraphMAE Cora-only; BGRL and GRACE-learnable-τ negative everywhere (learnable-τ = yet another pretraining-side failure, consistent with history).
35	- **Phase 9 KEY FINDING — probe quality ≠ ball quality**: CCA-SSG/GraphMAE H collapse to ONE ball (512-dim embeddings, geometry unsuitable for 2-means splitting); real-vs-shuffled gain vanishes; CiteSeer downstream worse than GRACE. **GRACE stays as main H — its InfoNCE uniformity makes it ball-splittable; linear separability alone doesn't transfer.** This "representation quality is two-dimensional (separability × clusterability)" finding is paper analysis material.
36	- **Phase 10 PubMed**: SoftDist beats NRGNN +2.4pp but loses to plain GCN+CE (-0.72pp); balls fine (64 balls, purity 0.81) but GCN+CE baseline too strong at 20% coverage on 3-class — correction cost > gain. PubMed = limitation/regime boundary. Amazon-Photo deferred (no official GRACE config; needs pre-registered fallback rule).
37	- **Phase 11 backbone**: ball increment positive on Cora for GAT/APPNP (3/3 seeds each) but negative/tied on CiteSeer → conditional appendix evidence only, no backbone-agnostic claim.
38	- **Net state: method = GRACE SoftDist [X||H] unchanged; CiteSeer gap to NRGNN stands; all four idea-lines (SSL swap, dataset, framework claim, backbone) resolved with honest boundaries. Paper positioning: Cora-regime strength + simplicity + noise-immune representation + rich negative-result analysis.**
39	
40	Update 2026-06-15 (paper-gap fills Phase 15-19 + custom SSL Phase 20 — all done, method unchanged):
41	- **Phase 15 instance noise**: ball contribution real at instance 0.4 (Cora +1.7pp/5/5, CiteSeer +1.5pp/4/5 over XH-CE), weak/negative at 0.2; NRGNN still wins CiteSeer. Strengthens "ball helps in higher-noise regime" claim.
42	- **Phase 16 coverage (current pipeline, replaces old C1 data)**: ball increment is NON-monotonic now — strongest at low coverage (Cora 0.05: +1.5pp), saturates/turns negative at high (Cora 0.40: -0.99pp). Because classifier now sees H directly via [X||H], part of old ball advantage is absorbed. Correct claim: balls help most when labels scarce enough that [X||H] hasn't saturated.
43	- **Phase 17 efficiency**: SoftDist 7.9s / 100k params / non-iterative vs NRGNN 24.7s / 465k / iterative (3.1× wall, 4.6× params); UnionNET timed out >1200s. Strong simplicity evidence. Must disclose amortizable H pretraining cost separately.
44	- **Phase 18 oracle gap-closure**: Cora 37.8%, CiteSeer 47.4%, PubMed -32.6% (boundary). Good paper context number.
45	- **Phase 19 Amazon-Photo (cross-domain)**: NOT a third success — real≈shuffled (ball-specific contribution absent), SoftDist≈GCN; but beats NRGNN +0.97pp/4/5. Balls did NOT collapse (64 balls, purity 0.86) — so it's a homophily/saturation boundary, not a geometry failure. Cross-domain boundary case.
46	- **Phase 20 custom SSL (GRACE+uniformity reg, label-free)**: FAILED geometry gate hard — explicit uniformity reg COLLAPSES balls to 1 on both datasets (purity 0.79→0.30), despite Cora unif0.1 probe slightly beating GRACE. Third confirmation of separability≠clusterability. Custom-SSL line closed; **GRACE's implicit alignment-uniformity balance is locally optimal for the recursive 2-means ball splitter** — strong "why GRACE" argument for §6.
47	- **Conclusion: every improvement axis exhausted (mechanism×7, gate-signal×3, SSL-method×4, SSL-objective×1, dataset×3, backbone×2, noise-type×3, coverage×4). Method is frozen. Only paper writing remains.**
48	
49	Update 2026-06-16 (Phase 24-27 fairness + 2025 external comparison — RESHAPES the core claim):
50	- **Phase 24 NRGNN [X||H] fairness control — the pivotal result**: gave NRGNN the SAME [X||H] input. Cora: NRGNN[X||H] 0.8139±0.0170 vs SoftDist 0.8137±0.0067 (delta -0.02pp, TIE). CiteSeer: NRGNN[X||H] 0.7090±0.0187 vs SoftDist 0.6891 (delta **-1.99pp, SoftDist LOSES**). **Implication: SoftDist does NOT beat a fully H-augmented strong baseline. Cannot claim "beats NRGNN" anymore.** Much of the apparent win was H, which any method can use.
51	- **BUT the ball-specific claim survives intact and is now cleaner**: SoftDist − GCN+CE[X||H] = +1.10/+1.30pp (4/5, 5/5); SoftDist − shuffled = +2.16/+1.95pp (5/5 both). I.e. given the same H, balls add real value over plain CE and over random balls. The honest positioning is **ball soft-targets as a simple, low-variance denoiser, NOT a SOTA-beater**.
52	- **Phase 25 TFR (CIKM 2025)**: ran same-protocol (DBLP template migrated to Cora/CiteSeer, NOT official tuned). Cora 0.7758 (loses to SoftDist -3.79pp), CiteSeer 0.6979 (SoftDist +0.88pp). Caveat: migrated config, not author-tuned — weak evidence.
53	- **Phase 26 ProCon**: no official code found → related-work only, no main-table row.
54	- **Phase 27 GD²**: not run, optional related-work citation.
55	- **Revised paper positioning (honest)**: drop "matches/beats NRGNN" headline. New frame = (1) simple non-iterative pipeline, lowest variance; (2) given identical H, ball soft-targets give real ball-specific gain over CE and random balls (the controlled, defensible claim); (3) H is noise-immune and reusable; (4) rich negative-result/mechanism-boundary analysis. The contribution is conceptual + efficiency + analysis, NOT raw SOTA. CiteSeer gap = NRGNN's online mechanism genuinely stronger once H is equalized.
56	
57	Update 2026-06-16 (Phase 28 DBLP dataset-breadth gate — NO-GO, confirms a STRONG boundary pattern):
58	- DBLP GRACE H fine (17716×256, aligned, row-norm 1.0) but **ball construction collapses to num_balls=1** (whole graph = 1 ball), CDR 0.55. SoftDist == shuffled exactly (0.8307) → ball structure contributes NOTHING; only H-as-feature helps. NRGNN[X||H] 0.8340 > SoftDist. **No-go: DBLP is not a 3rd success.**
59	- **The clustering-success pattern is now SHARP and dataset-typed**: ball structure gives real gain ONLY on the two small citation graphs Cora(2.7k,7cls)/CiteSeer(3.3k,6cls). It FAILS on every larger/denser graph tried: PubMed(19.7k,3cls, loses to GCN+CE), Amazon-Photo(7.6k, real≈shuffled), DBLP(17.7k, num_balls=1 total collapse). This is no longer "a couple boundaries" — it's a **systematic limit: SoftDist's granular-ball benefit is confined to small low-class-count citation graphs where GRACE H is locally clusterable.**
60	- **Honest implication for paper**: only 2 datasets show the ball-specific effect. This is the single biggest weakness. The dataset-breadth axis is now also EXHAUSTED downward (DBLP was the most-favorable untried homophilous graph and it collapsed). Remaining options are narrow: (a) accept 2-dataset scope + frame as focused contribution + heavy mechanism analysis (KBS/Neural Networks viable, top-venue hard); (b) investigate WHY GRACE H clusters on Cora/CiteSeer but not larger graphs (ball construction params? embedding dim? graph density?) — this is a real open question, not yet ruled out. Report: `runs/dblp_20260616/dblp_phase28_report.md`.
61	
62	Update 2026-06-16 (Phase 32 big-graph ball-scaling diagnostic — splits the boundary into TWO layers, resolves option (b)):
63	- **32a (construction layer)**: DBLP `num_balls=1` was PARAMETER MISFIT, not intrinsic. With `split_improvement` lowered (0.001-0.005) + `max_balls=256`, DBLP/PubMed/Amazon-Photo all reach true_purity 0.83-0.87, EXCEEDING Cora/CiteSeer's 0.70-0.79. So "large-graph H is not clusterable" is FALSE — geometric balls recover fine with scaled params.
64	- **32b (downstream layer)**: BUT even with high-purity recovered balls, DBLP/PubMed/Amazon-Photo still show NO ball-specific gain — Real−Shuffled = -0.83/-0.37/-0.04pp (all ≤0), Real−GCN[X||H] ≈ +0.0pp. High purity ≠ downstream gain (echoes Phase 9 lesson again).
65	- **The refined, deeper finding**: the limit is NOT "balls can't form on big graphs" — they form fine and are pure. The limit is that **on larger/denser graphs the ball-induced noisy-label target adds nothing beyond what the H feature already gives the classifier** (gain absorbed by [X||H] input or training noise). The ball-specific denoising effect is genuinely confined to small citation graphs (Cora/CiteSeer); this is now a clean two-layer boundary (construction OK, downstream contribution absorbed), not a parameter bug.
66	- **Option (b) is now CLOSED**: dataset breadth cannot be rescued by parameter tuning. Scope is firmly 2 datasets for the ball-specific claim. Paper = focused contribution + the two-layer boundary analysis is itself a strong honest result. Report: `runs/bigball_downstream_20260616/bigball_phase32_report.md`. **Every axis now exhausted including dataset-breadth-via-params. Method frozen, paper-writing only.**
67	
68	Update 2026-06-16 (Phase 33-34 big-graph clean-sample-selection — strong offline signal but downstream NO-GO; the命门对照 saved us):
69	- Phase 33 offline looked very promising: ball noise-discrimination conditionally orthogonal to GCN (ball-AUC-in-GCN-clean50 = 0.66-0.95 all pass), co-teaching intersection drops train noise 40%→6% keeping ~53%. Looked like dataset breadth unlocked.
70	- **Phase 34 downstream KILLED it via the pre-registered命门对照 (gbselect vs gcn_only)**: the whole value of co-teaching is "ball 2nd view beats GCN single view". Result:
71	  - DBLP: real>shuffled (+4.7pp, 5/5) ✓ but **gbselect vs gcn_only unstable** (keep0.6 -0.04pp 1/5, keep0.7 +0.35pp only 3/5 < 4/5 gate). Weak.
72	  - PubMed: real>shuffled ✓ but **gbselect vs gcn_only +0.06pp 2/5 FAIL** — cleaner subset cancelled by sample-loss + GCN's own filtering ability.
73	  - Amazon-Photo: **gbselect>gcn_only +3.1pp 5/5 PASS the gate, BUT gbselect −12.3pp BELOW full-train GCN[X||H]** — selection throws away too much supervision; plain GCN already strong.
74	- **Deep finding**: balls genuinely carry orthogonal noise info (offline + real>shuffled everywhere confirm it), but on big graphs that info CANNOT convert to downstream gain — three independent killers: (1) sample-loss from selection > denoising benefit, (2) GCN single-view already filters most of what balls catch, (3) big-graph baselines already strong. The命门对照 prevented falsely claiming success from the Amazon "5/5 vs gcn_only" without noticing it lost 12pp to plain baseline.
75	- **DEFINITIVE conclusion: every form of using balls on big graphs is exhausted — soft-target (32), and selection (34). The ball-specific benefit is intrinsically confined to small citation graphs (Cora/CiteSeer).** Report: `runs/gbselect_20260616/gbselect_phase34_report.md`. Paper = focused 2-dataset contribution + unusually thorough boundary analysis (soft-target fails big AND selection fails big, both diagnosed). Mechanism exploration TRULY done.
76	
77	Update 2026-06-16 (Phase 35 size×class boundary — "big graph fails" OVERTURNED; scope expands to 3 datasets):
78	- The "only small graphs work" conclusion above was WRONG — it confounded size with class-count. All prior datasets sat on the diagonal (big ones happened to be few-class). Phase 35 broke the confound with a discriminative point: **Coauthor-CS (18.3k nodes, 15 classes) — same size as DBLP (17.7k) but many classes.**
79	- **Coauthor-CS SUCCEEDS**: SoftDist[X||H] 0.9243 vs GCN[X||H] 0.9190 (+0.53pp 5/5) vs shuffled +0.55pp 5/5. GBSelect also passes命门 (vs gcn_only +0.71pp 4/5, vs full-train +0.67pp 5/5). ball_auc_in_gcn_clean50=0.85, purity 0.91. → **class-count, not graph size, is the governing variable. Big graphs are NOT excluded.**
80	- **Amazon-Computers (13.7k, 10 classes) refines it**: real>shuffled holds (+1.8pp 5/5, ball signal real) BUT SoftDist −0.70pp below GCN[X||H] (strong homophily 0.79 + strong baseline 0.87 absorbs it). So class-count is necessary-ish but NOT sufficient — graph regime / baseline strength still matters.
81	- **NEW scope: success datasets = Cora / CiteSeer / Coauthor-CS (3 now, was 2).** Honest claim: "size is not the death cause; class complexity / label-noise separability is the key modulating variable, but strong-homophily regimes with already-strong [X||H] baselines can still absorb the ball signal." This is a MUCH better story than "only 2 small graphs."
82	- cora3c (Q1) deferred — Q2 already broke the confound; cora3c is now low marginal value, optional appendix.
83	- **Next: if Coauthor-CS enters main table, needs NRGNN/baseline完整 5-seed on it. Then paper-writing.** Report: `runs/size_class_boundary_20260616/phase35_size_class_boundary_report.md`.
84	
85	Update 2026-06-17 (Phase 36 Coauthor-CS into main table + 2D boundary fig — DONE, paper格局 upgraded):
86	- Coauthor-CS full baselines (5-seed, uniform 0.4): GCN+CE 0.9196, GCN[X||H] 0.9190, NRGNN 0.9356, NRGNN[X||H] **0.9366**, SoftDist[X||H] 0.9243, shuffled 0.9188. Ball gains hold: SoftDist−GCN[X||H] +0.53pp 5/5, SoftDist−shuffled +0.55pp 5/5. BUT SoftDist−NRGNN[X||H] −1.23pp 0/5 (loses, same pattern as CiteSeer).
87	- Amazon-Computers baselines: GCN[X||H] 0.8695 (best), SoftDist 0.8625, NRGNN[X||H] 0.8230. SoftDist beats shuffled +1.8pp 5/5 AND beats NRGNN[X||H] +3.95pp 5/5, but loses to full-train GCN[X||H] −0.70pp → boundary point (ball signal real, absorbed by strong baseline).
88	- **Final dataset story: 3 success datasets (Cora/CiteSeer/Coauthor-CS) where ball gain is stable 5/5 over GCN[X||H] and shuffled. Coauthor-CS = 18k-node big graph → kills "only small graphs" concern. 2D size×class boundary figure done: ball helps when class-count high enough (task hard enough that GCN single-view can't filter noise alone) AND baseline not already saturated (Amazon regime absorbs).**
89	- Honest position holds: SoftDist ties NRGNN[X||H] on Cora, loses on CiteSeer & Coauthor-CS. Contribution = simplicity + non-iterative + controlled ball gain + 2D applicability characterization, NOT SOTA. Paper draft §3/§4/§8 all backfilled, boundary fig at `runs/figures_20260617/size_class_boundary.png`.
90	- **Experiments now genuinely complete: 3 success datasets + full external baselines + 2D boundary + exhaustive negative-result/mechanism analysis. Next = paper writing.**

92	Update 2026-06-17 (Phase 37 multivariate applicability grid — KEY FINDING: orthogonal-AUC / ball-purity is the governing label-free variable):
93	- 9-dataset grid (added Coauthor-Physics 34.5k/5cls/h0.93, WikiCS 11.7k/10cls/h0.65). Measured 5 candidate variables (N, C, homophily, noise-harm, orthogonal-AUC) vs ball gain.
94	- **The decisive correlation: GBSelect gain vs orthogonal_AUC / ball_AUC / true_ball_purity = Spearman 1.00 (Pearson 0.94-0.97), n=4. SoftDist gain vs orthogonal_AUC Pearson 0.99, ball_purity 0.97.** Surface variables far weaker: classes Spearman -0.67~0.20, nodes -0.37~-0.50, homophily 0.40-0.43, noise_harm 0.31-0.70. **→ ball-clusterability (purity/orthogonal-AUC), NOT size/class/homophily, is what governs whether balls help.** size×class was a proxy; the real variable is whether H forms pure balls.
95	- WikiCS (h=0.65 medium, 10 classes) is a clean negative confirmation: orthogonal_AUC 0.528 (near-random), and ball gain NEGATIVE everywhere (SoftDist -0.87pp, GBSelect-gcn_only -4.25pp). Low orthogonal AUC → balls hurt. Perfect monotone with the governing variable.
96	- **Adaptive-layer verdict (correcting Codex's "no deployable trigger")**: true_ball_purity and orthogonal_AUC are computed from H-geometry + train-NOISY labels only — they are NOT clean-label-dependent (homophily/noise-harm are, those can't deploy). Ball-purity especially is fully label-free-ish (only noisy train). So a deploy-time adaptive trigger λ=f(ball_purity/orthogonal_AUC) IS feasible in principle — Codex conflated the genuinely-clean-only vars (homophily, noise_harm) with the noisy-train-computable ones (ball_purity, orthogonal_AUC). This is the strongest result for 想法2 yet, but n=4-5 is tiny — needs more points before claiming a deployable law.
97	- Report: `runs/applicability_grid_20260617/correlation_analysis.md`.

100	- Tested ONLY deploy-time proxies (H + noisy train labels, no clean): noisy_train_purity, vote margin/entropy, eligible ratio, num_balls, mean_train_per_ball, ball-GCN disagreement.
101	- 37d-pre passed: noisy purity NOT washed flat (range 0.226-0.553 across datasets), WikiCS lowest (0.226) consistent with it failing — so noisy purity has discriminative potential.
102	- Top correlations look strong: GBSelect gain vs ball_gcn_disagree_confident_train Spearman -1.00 (n=5), vs mean_vote_margin +0.83 (n=6); SoftDist gain vs mean_ball_size/mean_train_per_ball -1.00 (n=5). Disagreement & vote-margin are genuinely deploy-able and point the right way (low disagreement / high margin → ball helps).
103	- **BUT pre-registered gate was n≥7; largest sample is n=6 → run is UNDERPOWERED, cannot legally pass/fail.** Also Spearman=±1.00 at n=5 is statistically near-meaningless (5 points trivially monotone). Several configs missing (coauthorph H missing, gbselect missing for cora/citeseer) shrank n.
104	- **Verdict: adaptive-layer neither confirmed nor killed. To decide, must (a) fill missing target deltas — coauthorph GRACE H + gbselect on cora/citeseer, (b) get n≥8-10. Until then: deploy-able proxies (vote-margin, ball-GCN-disagreement) are PROMISING candidate triggers, not established.**
105	- claim discipline holds: only "evidence suggests ball-clusterability mediates ball gains"; n-limit stated everywhere. Report: `runs/deployable_proxy_20260617/deployable_proxy_report.md`.
106	
107	Update 2026-06-18 (Phase 39 LastFM-Asia + noise-breadth 0.5 — both confirm boundary theory, success set stays 3):
108	- **LastFM-Asia (7.6k, 18 classes): BOUNDARY, not 4th success — diagnostic先行 stopped it before downstream.** Despite 18 classes (passed class-count condition), it FAILED 2/3 gates: true_ball_purity 0.254 (<0.65), orthogonal_AUC 0.600 (<0.70). Why: country labels vs music-interest (artist) geometry are weakly aligned → H-balls aren't label-pure; AND homophily 0.874 (>0.85) → early GCN noise-AUC 0.951 already separates noise, leaving no orthogonal room for balls. **Confirms class-count is necessary-not-sufficient; the real mediator is ball label-purity (geometry-label alignment), exactly the §8.1f thesis. Data caveat: PyG npz 404'd, used deterministic SNAP reconstruction (SVD-128), protocol-compatible not byte-identical — note in paper.**
109	- **Noise-breadth 0.5 filled (150 rows, all 3 success datasets + pair/instance):** Cora uniform 0.5 SoftDist−GCN[X||H] +1.52pp 5/5 (strongest uniform point!), CiteSeer +0.83pp 4/5, Coauthor-CS smaller. Confirms the bell-shape: ball gain peaks mid-high noise (0.4-0.5), collapses at 0.6 (Cora 0.6 real<shuffled). pair 0.6 correctly excluded (designated wrong-class becomes majority above 0.5).
110	- **pair noise weakness now systematic across datasets**: pair 0.2 unstable everywhere, pair 0.4 retain on Cora but "no stable increment" on CiteSeer/Coauthor-CS. Mechanism (false-majority from systematic A→B flips) + future-work fix (H-geometry validates noisy majority) recorded in Phase 39 report.
111	- **Final stable picture: 3 controlled-success datasets (Cora/CiteSeer/Coauthor-CS), 5+ boundary datasets all mechanistically explained by ball label-purity. Noise spectrum: uniform full 0.2-0.6 on success sets, pair/instance covered. Experiments truly complete. → paper writing.** Reports: `runs/lastfmasia_20260618/phase39_result.md`, `runs/noise_breadth_20260618/noise_robustness_report.md`.
112	
113	Update 2026-06-18 (SoftDist-MLP line — strong positive, X-ball negative, monotone weakness-rule established):
114	- **Dual-positioning confirmed (主性能=SoftDist-GCN[X||H]; 机制轻量变体=SoftDist-MLP(X)).** The ball-gain-vs-downstream-strength MONOTONE rule is now the cleanest mechanism evidence: GCN[X||H] ~+1pp (absorbed) < GCN(X) +1.1/+2.1pp < **MLP(X) +6 to +9pp**. Weaker/H-free/no-message-passing downstream → larger ball margin.
115	- **MLP noise spectrum (180 rows, both datasets 6/6 stable):** SoftDist-MLP(X) beats CE AND shuffled at clean(safe, +0.4/+2.1pp), uniform 0.2/0.4/0.5/0.6, pair 0.4, instance 0.4 — ALL stable 4-5/5. Surprise: the +8pp is NOT a uniform-0.4 sweet spot; it's broad across noise types/rates on weak MLP. Even uniform 0.6 holds (+6.8/+3.5pp) — opposite of GCN where 0.6 collapses (because MLP+CE baseline already so low there's room). Claim limited to "transfers to X-only MLP", NOT model-independent (GAT CiteSeer −1.22pp, APPNP −0.16pp negatives PRESERVED).
116	- **Efficiency table (downstream only, GRACE excluded):** SoftDist-MLP 92k params / 5.7s / 140MiB vs NRGNN 465k / 29s / 406MiB vs SoftDist-GCN[X||H] 100k / 4.9s. Ball-target build ~2.5-5.7s is the main SoftDist downstream cost. Can say "lightweight downstream" NOT "end-to-end win" (GRACE cost real).
117	- **X-ball (完全无H) FAILED preregistered gate cleanly:** raw-X-space geometry collapses to num_balls=1 (purity 0.30/0.21, CDR 0.68/0.78), real==shuffled, downstream NOT run per stopping rule. **Confirms H/GRACE is NECESSARY for ball construction — raw X is not clusterable. Settles the "can we drop H entirely" question: NO.** Topology-ball left as separate future preregistration (not run).
118	- GPT corrections accepted: (1) GCN(X)+SoftDist already proved "no-H-to-classifier" 5月, MLP is the extreme point of a rule not a standalone proof; (2) "model-independent" overclaim — keep GAT/APPNP negatives; (3) success condition is noise_harm + ball-noise-detection + ball-GCN orthogonality (Phase 37 evidence), not "find weak-GCN dataset" from scratch. Reports: `runs/softdist_mlp_noise_spectrum_20260618/`, `runs/softdist_mlp_efficiency_20260618/`, `runs/featuregb_mlp_diagnostic_20260618/`.
119	
120	Update 2026-06-17 (Phase 38 evidence-matrix, frozen 3 proxies, n filled to 7-8 — adaptive layer NOT supported, deferred to future work):
121	- Filled holes (gbselect on Cora/CiteSeer + NA deltas; Coauthor-Physics H still missing). Max n reached = 8 (< pre-registered 10 bar). Adaptive layer NOT evaluated → future work, per discipline.
122	- **Frozen-proxy honest correlations (the 37d "Spearman=1.00" was an n=5 artifact — collapsed once n grew):** best is GBSelect-gain vs mean_vote_entropy_weighted Spearman -0.79 (n=8), vs mean_vote_margin_weighted +0.67 (n=8). SoftDist-gain correlations weak (|Spearman|≤0.57). ball_gcn_disagree (the 37d star at -1.00/n=5) collapsed to -0.54/n=7. → proxies are PROMISING-but-not-robust at n≤8; vote-entropy/margin point the right way (purer balls → more ball gain) but below any deployable bar.
123	- **Verdict: adaptive layer stays future work. Deployable-proxy evidence is preliminary.** This actually STRENGTHENS the paper's honesty: we tested, reported frozen proxies without cherry-picking, found the earlier perfect correlation was small-sample noise.
124	- **Experiments are now DONE. No open mechanism/dataset/proxy axis with positive ROI remains.** Final paper assets: 3 success datasets (Cora/CiteSeer/Coauthor-CS incl 18k big graph) + full external baselines (NRGNN/NRGNN[X||H]/TFR/5 NoisyGL methods) + [X||H] attribution chain + shuffled controls + 2D size×class boundary + ball-clusterability mediation evidence (diagnostic vars strong, deployable proxies preliminary) + exhaustive negative results (mechanism×7, gate×3, SSL×4, big-graph soft-target/selection, adaptive-proxy). Honest positioning: simple non-iterative pipeline, controlled ball gain, thorough applicability+boundary characterization, NOT SOTA. → PAPER WRITING.
125	- Run protocol gotcha: NoisyGL ratio split needs explicit `--split_type percent --train_percent 0.2 --val_percent 0.1 --test_percent 0.7` on single_exp.py, else it silently falls back to Planetoid default (140 train on Cora). ROCm python: `Desktop/三论文融合/三论文融合/GRACE-master/.venv-rocm/Scripts/python.exe`.

---
name: gb-direction-turning-point-2026-06
description: Noisy-label GB research pivoted from graph-aware ball to reliable mutual-kNN ball on contrastive representation
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: ba7cc747-3543-45ef-8091-c58dddb44384
---

As of 2026-06-07 the noisy-label-robust node-classification project (Cora/CiteSeer, no heterophilous graphs) made a confirmed direction pivot, recorded in `02_experiment_history_and_lessons.md` §12 and `external/NoisyGL/runs/orgingb_noisygl_experiment_history_20260604.md` §9.

Three evidence-backed conclusions:
1. **Graph-aware granular ball is dropped as a headline novelty** — on Cora/CiteSeer the topology increment `dcgb − dcgb_emb_only` is ±0.001 (purity/AUROC) across all 8 conditions; adjacency is redundant with features/GRACE on homophilous graphs.
2. **Reciprocal mutual-kNN reliable ball is the real positive signal** — ordinary GB purity collapses on raw features (Cora 0.30) while mutual-kNN balls recover it (0.78–0.84); AUROC over `gb` beats baseline with non-overlapping std in 4/4 settings.
3. **Supervised GCN representation is unreliable under label noise** — S1 (ReliableGB-GCN reweight) ties GCN (0.705, best_phase=warmup) because GCN val peaks ~epoch 6 then memorizes noise; this motivates building the same reliable balls on a label-free contrastive representation.

Candidate paper mainline: **label-free contrastive representation + mutual-kNN reliable granular ball + conservative noise-aware training** (NOT graph-aware).

Update 2026-06-10 (frozen-GRACE-ball + fresh end-to-end GCN line, NoisyGL percent split 0.2/0.1/0.7 uniform 0.4):
- **SoftDist is the confirmed best mechanism**: geometric balls on frozen GRACE H + multiclass-alpha ball-distribution soft targets + fresh GCN. 5-seed: Cora 0.795±0.009 (GCN+CE 0.784), CiteSeer 0.674±0.011 (GCN+CE 0.653); beats shuffled everywhere; loses to NRGNN (0.811/0.703) by ~1.5-3pp.
- **Failed add-ons (all seed0-refuted)**: dynamic alpha (self-reinforcing), ball-consistency regularizer, NRGNN+BallAux (ball signal redundant with graph propagation), and E1 label-aware adaptive granularity.
- **E1 negative result (2026-06-10)**: purity-coverage adaptive ball splitting (3 variants: threshold/strict-gain/multi-attempt-gain) cannot beat geometric balls at 20% coverage — per-ball noisy purity estimates (5-15 votes, noise ceiling ~0.66, std ~0.15) are too weak to drive granularity; CDR never dropped. Report: `external/NoisyGL/runs/adaptive_gb_seed0_rocm_20260610/adaptive_gb_e1_seed0_rocm_report_20260610.md`. E2 (unlabeled expansion on adaptive purity) cancelled with it.
- **Decided fallback: Route A** — paper positions SoftDist as first GB mechanism for noisy-label node classification + coverage sensitivity + mechanism-boundary negative results; do not chase NRGNN on its home regime.

Update 2026-06-11 (XH mainline confirmed, 5-seed):
- **SoftDist [X||H] is the new mainline**: concat row-L2-normalized GRACE H onto GCN input features + SoftDist ball targets. 5-seed: Cora **0.8137±0.0067 (≥ NRGNN 0.8107±0.0230, 3× lower std)**, CiteSeer 0.6891±0.0159 (NRGNN 0.7027, gap -1.36pp). Full ablation chain clean: H-on-CE +1.9/+2.3pp, ball-on-H +1.1/+1.3pp, real>shuffled 5/5 both datasets. Cora seed0 (ball-on-H negative) was misleading.
- Phase 4a early-learning arbitration diagnostic FAILED its gates (Cora: too few protected; CiteSeer: protection precision 48-68% < 70%). X-only warmup recheck (4a-2) also failed identically → **Phase 4 permanently closed**; clean mechanism boundary: early-learning confidence (coupled or independent of H) cannot safely protect clean labels in this pipeline.
- **Noise grid regime analysis done (2026-06-11)**: no strict regime win vs NRGNN. Cora = tie in 4/5 regimes (competitive, lower variance); CiteSeer = loss everywhere; uniform 0.6 = big loss (offline correction breaks down, NRGNN online mechanism wins; Cora real even loses to shuffled there). Ball increment peaks at uniform 0.4 / pair 0.4; redundant at low noise. Report: `runs/noise_grid_rocm_20260611/`.
- **Mechanism exploration is CONCLUDED.** Final method = SoftDist [X||H]. Paper claims: (1) simple non-iterative GB pipeline competitive with NRGNN on Cora with 3× lower variance, (2) label-noise-immune representation stage (same H reused across all regimes), (3) clean attribution chain, (4) honest applicability boundary (CiteSeer, high uniform noise) + five mechanism-boundary negative results. Next work is paper writing, not more mechanisms.

Update 2026-06-12 (literature mining closed): 13 GB+DL papers audited — 12 re-skins of closed directions or domain-mismatched; the survivor (MGNR multi-granularity consistency gate) failed preregistered gates (protection precision 0.52 < 0.70 — cross-scale disagreement marks vote ambiguity, not clean-label boundaries). **Three independent gate signals now refuted: vote-count, temporal, scale** — clean-vs-noisy is inseparable among ball-correction candidates at 20% coverage / 40% noise. Report: `runs/multigranularity_diag_20260612/`.

Update 2026-06-12 (Phase 8-11 SSL upgrade / dataset / backbone — all four resolved):
- **Phase 8 probe**: CCA-SSG beat GRACE probe on both datasets (+2.7/+1.6pp clean); GraphMAE Cora-only; BGRL and GRACE-learnable-τ negative everywhere (learnable-τ = yet another pretraining-side failure, consistent with history).
- **Phase 9 KEY FINDING — probe quality ≠ ball quality**: CCA-SSG/GraphMAE H collapse to ONE ball (512-dim embeddings, geometry unsuitable for 2-means splitting); real-vs-shuffled gain vanishes; CiteSeer downstream worse than GRACE. **GRACE stays as main H — its InfoNCE uniformity makes it ball-splittable; linear separability alone doesn't transfer.** This "representation quality is two-dimensional (separability × clusterability)" finding is paper analysis material.
- **Phase 10 PubMed**: SoftDist beats NRGNN +2.4pp but loses to plain GCN+CE (-0.72pp); balls fine (64 balls, purity 0.81) but GCN+CE baseline too strong at 20% coverage on 3-class — correction cost > gain. PubMed = limitation/regime boundary. Amazon-Photo deferred (no official GRACE config; needs pre-registered fallback rule).
- **Phase 11 backbone**: ball increment positive on Cora for GAT/APPNP (3/3 seeds each) but negative/tied on CiteSeer → conditional appendix evidence only, no backbone-agnostic claim.
- **Net state: method = GRACE SoftDist [X||H] unchanged; CiteSeer gap to NRGNN stands; all four idea-lines (SSL swap, dataset, framework claim, backbone) resolved with honest boundaries. Paper positioning: Cora-regime strength + simplicity + noise-immune representation + rich negative-result analysis.**

Update 2026-06-15 (paper-gap fills Phase 15-19 + custom SSL Phase 20 — all done, method unchanged):
- **Phase 15 instance noise**: ball contribution real at instance 0.4 (Cora +1.7pp/5/5, CiteSeer +1.5pp/4/5 over XH-CE), weak/negative at 0.2; NRGNN still wins CiteSeer. Strengthens "ball helps in higher-noise regime" claim.
- **Phase 16 coverage (current pipeline, replaces old C1 data)**: ball increment is NON-monotonic now — strongest at low coverage (Cora 0.05: +1.5pp), saturates/turns negative at high (Cora 0.40: -0.99pp). Because classifier now sees H directly via [X||H], part of old ball advantage is absorbed. Correct claim: balls help most when labels scarce enough that [X||H] hasn't saturated.
- **Phase 17 efficiency**: SoftDist 7.9s / 100k params / non-iterative vs NRGNN 24.7s / 465k / iterative (3.1× wall, 4.6× params); UnionNET timed out >1200s. Strong simplicity evidence. Must disclose amortizable H pretraining cost separately.
- **Phase 18 oracle gap-closure**: Cora 37.8%, CiteSeer 47.4%, PubMed -32.6% (boundary). Good paper context number.
- **Phase 19 Amazon-Photo (cross-domain)**: NOT a third success — real≈shuffled (ball-specific contribution absent), SoftDist≈GCN; but beats NRGNN +0.97pp/4/5. Balls did NOT collapse (64 balls, purity 0.86) — so it's a homophily/saturation boundary, not a geometry failure. Cross-domain boundary case.
- **Phase 20 custom SSL (GRACE+uniformity reg, label-free)**: FAILED geometry gate hard — explicit uniformity reg COLLAPSES balls to 1 on both datasets (purity 0.79→0.30), despite Cora unif0.1 probe slightly beating GRACE. Third confirmation of separability≠clusterability. Custom-SSL line closed; **GRACE's implicit alignment-uniformity balance is locally optimal for the recursive 2-means ball splitter** — strong "why GRACE" argument for §6.
- **Conclusion: every improvement axis exhausted (mechanism×7, gate-signal×3, SSL-method×4, SSL-objective×1, dataset×3, backbone×2, noise-type×3, coverage×4). Method is frozen. Only paper writing remains.**

Update 2026-06-16 (Phase 24-27 fairness + 2025 external comparison — RESHAPES the core claim):
- **Phase 24 NRGNN [X||H] fairness control — the pivotal result**: gave NRGNN the SAME [X||H] input. Cora: NRGNN[X||H] 0.8139±0.0170 vs SoftDist 0.8137±0.0067 (delta -0.02pp, TIE). CiteSeer: NRGNN[X||H] 0.7090±0.0187 vs SoftDist 0.6891 (delta **-1.99pp, SoftDist LOSES**). **Implication: SoftDist does NOT beat a fully H-augmented strong baseline. Cannot claim "beats NRGNN" anymore.** Much of the apparent win was H, which any method can use.
- **BUT the ball-specific claim survives intact and is now cleaner**: SoftDist − GCN+CE[X||H] = +1.10/+1.30pp (4/5, 5/5); SoftDist − shuffled = +2.16/+1.95pp (5/5 both). I.e. given the same H, balls add real value over plain CE and over random balls. The honest positioning is **ball soft-targets as a simple, low-variance denoiser, NOT a SOTA-beater**.
- **Phase 25 TFR (CIKM 2025)**: ran same-protocol (DBLP template migrated to Cora/CiteSeer, NOT official tuned). Cora 0.7758 (loses to SoftDist -3.79pp), CiteSeer 0.6979 (SoftDist +0.88pp). Caveat: migrated config, not author-tuned — weak evidence.
- **Phase 26 ProCon**: no official code found → related-work only, no main-table row.
- **Phase 27 GD²**: not run, optional related-work citation.
- **Revised paper positioning (honest)**: drop "matches/beats NRGNN" headline. Update 2026-06-30 (★MAJOR PIVOT — graph line fully closed, project moves off graphs entirely★):
After 45 days total (NOT a year), the entire "granular-ball + graph (GRACE H + GCN)" line is CLOSED across four tasks, each pre-registered and honestly killed:
1. **classification (Phase 24)**: SoftDist ties/loses to NRGNN once given same [X‖H] — not SOTA.
2. **noise detection (Phase 39 detection variant)**: ball LOO AUROC strong (0.83-0.96) but DOMINATED by kNN-in-H/GCN-conf; corr(ball,kNN-in-H)=0.78-0.90 → ball = coarsened kNN-in-H.
3. **cross-view conflict (Phase 40)**: reversed — conflict nodes are CLEANER; conditional AUROC far below two-kNN union. NO-GO.
4. **K-free ball graph clustering (Phase 41)**: GB cluster ACC 10-15pp BELOW kmeans-fed-true-K; G4 fails (ball aggregation ≤ kmeans-on-auto-K, ball step redundant/negative). NO-GO.

**Unifying root cause (the "higher-dimension ruler", the single most valuable lesson)**: `ball value = max(0, structure ball provides − structure the downstream/simple method already gets)`. On graph+strong-self-supervised-rep (GRACE H), balls do "local statistics" that kNN-in-H/GCN-conf/kmeans already do, equal or better. Graph nodes + strong rep + adjacency prior = the WORST battlefield for balls.

**Why CGBC/GBmooer (the originals being imitated) succeed but SoftDist didn't**: theirs are END-TO-END (ball loss reshapes encoder) with WEAK downstream lacking local structure; SoftDist is FROZEN-H + decoupled fresh GCN (ball outside gradient flow) with STRONG downstream. NO successful GB+DL paper among 145 reviewed uses "frozen rep + offline ball" single-pass流水线.

**NEW DIRECTION (chosen, user committed)**: **open intent / open-set / OOD recognition** — balls model "known-class multi-granularity local boundary + uncertainty geometry + unknown rejection"; ball signal participates dynamically in training (curriculum/confidence scheduling), not static post-processing. Why open-set: the task INTRINSICALLY needs ball strengths (radius=coverage, overlap=fuzzy boundary, density=uncertainty); NLP open-intent (CLINC150/BANKING77) has ready BERT embeddings (fits 2-month/5-6wk window on 7700XT); group has a starting point (MOGB) but uncertainty-geometry not done. Eval switches to AUROC/FPR95/unknown-F1/macro-F1/ECE (NOT accuracy).

**★THE non-negotiable first gate carried into the new domain (the 45-day moat)★**: before writing any full method, run a KILL TEST — does the ball uncertainty/rejection/difficulty signal provide CONDITIONAL GAIN over standard simple OOD signals (MSP/Energy/Mahalanobis/prototype-dist/kNN-OOD), NOT just be a re-skin? Judged like Phase 39 conditional-AUROC: within the subset where the simple signal already "handles" samples, can the ball still add independent value? Pass → real new role; fail → re-skin (5th absorption), pivot to backup domain. (Codex's correction: criterion is residual/conditional gain + replacement-ablation, NOT zero correlation — radius/density correlating with loss/conf is normal.)

Full handoff with idea design, algorithm, 145-paper essence, and red lines: `开放意图粒球新方向0630/HANDOFF_交接文件.md`. The 145-paper unifying formula: "ball = adaptive local unit in any representation space, attached to some downstream; the 145 only ever vary the downstream and the rep-space." Ball's three (only three) contributions: compression (exclusive), local-robust-statistic (NON-exclusive — kNN re-skins it, this was the death cause, user over-invested here), adaptive-no-K granularity (exclusive). New direction should bet on a 4th NEW role (uncertainty geometry / training-dynamics scheduler), not contribution #2.

---

## 给网页版 GPT 的 Deep-Research 提示词

（直接复制下面整段发给网页 GPT。它没有我们的上下文，所以提示词里我把必要背景压缩进去了。）

---

我在做一个研究方向的可行性调研，目标是**用"粒球计算（granular ball computing）"在开放意图识别 / 开放集识别 / OOD 检测中，建模已知类的多粒度局部边界与不确定性，并据此做未知样本拒识**。我需要你做一次深入的、带来源 URL 的文献调研，重点不是泛泛综述，而是为我设计一个"对照实验"提供精确的靶子。请务必基于真实可检索的文献，凡引用具体方法/数据/数字都附 URL，不确定的明确标注。

请系统回答以下问题：

**1. 开放意图识别（open intent / open-set intent detection, NLP）的标准方法与评测**
- 近 3-4 年（2022-2026）代表方法有哪些（如 ADB、DA-ADB、(K+1)-way、DeepUnk、MSP-based、KNNCL、各种基于 BERT/Sentence-BERT 的方法）？
- 标准数据集：CLINC150、BANKING77、StackOverflow、SNIPS、OOS 等——各自规模、已知/未知类划分协议（known class ratio 25%/50%/75%）。
- 标准评测指标：accuracy、macro-F1、known-F1、unknown-F1、AUROC、FPR95 等，分别怎么算。

**2. ★最关键★：开放集/OOD 的"标准不确定性打分函数"全集（这是我要对照的 baseline）**
我需要一份尽量完整的"post-hoc / 打分式" OOD/unknown 检测方法清单，每个给出：打分公式的直觉、需要什么输入（logits / 特征 / 训练集）、是否 post-hoc。至少覆盖：
- MSP（max softmax probability，Hendrycks）
- Energy score（Liu et al.）
- Mahalanobis distance（Lee et al.）
- ODIN
- 单 prototype / 类中心距离
- kNN-based OOD（Sun et al. "Out-of-distribution detection with deep nearest neighbors"）
- ViM、ReAct、KNN+、GEN 等较新的
- 以及开放意图领域特有的 adaptive decision boundary（ADB/DA-ADB）
对每个，请说明它本质上用的是"哪一种几何/统计信息"（softmax 置信度 / 能量 / 到类中心距离 / 局部密度 / k 近邻距离），因为我要证明我的"粒球不确定性信号"提供了它们之外的**条件增益**。

**3. 粒球（granular ball）在 open-set / open-intent / OOD 中的现状与空位**
- 有没有论文已经把粒球用于 open intent / open-set / OOD？（已知一篇 MOGB：Multi-Granularity Open Intent Classification via Adaptive Granular-Ball Decision Boundary；另有 BNO-GB：Beneficial Noise learning for open intent classification, Pattern Recognition 2026。请核实它们到底做了什么、用什么数据、和"粒球做多粒度不确定性几何 + post-hoc 拒识打分"的区别在哪。）
- 除这两篇外还有没有别的粒球+open-set 工作？如果几乎没有，这就是空位。

**4. "多粒度 / 局部覆盖 / 半径密度"类方法在 OOD 中的相关工作**
- 有没有非粒球但思想相近的工作（如基于多个 prototype、多中心、局部密度、覆盖球/hypersphere 的 OOD/open-set 方法，例如 deep hypersphere、SLPN、多原型拒识）？这些是我必须区分和对照的近亲。

**5. 如果要立论点，最可能立得住的差异化点 + 最大风险**
- 一个"粒球做已知类多粒度局部边界 + 不确定性几何 + 拒识"的方法，相比 MSP/Energy/Maha/kNN-OOD/ADB，最可能立得住的差异化论点是什么？
- 最大风险是什么（尤其：粒球的拒识分数会不会其实等价于"到最近类中心距离"或"kNN 距离"的换皮）？

**6. 实验设计建议**
- 如果要做一个"粒球不确定性信号 vs 标准 OOD 打分"的对照实验，标准数据集、已知/未知划分、必报指标、必须对照的 baseline 分别是什么？
- 在 16GB 单卡（消费级 GPU）上，用 BERT-base 做这个实验的可行性和典型计算量。

请把回答组织成结构化报告，每个关键论断附 URL。最后给一个明确结论：这个方向（粒球做 open-set 不确定性几何）**值得做 / 有条件值得做 / 不值得做**，以及"有条件"的话条件是什么。

---

## 流程确认

1. ✅ 交接文件：`开放意图粒球新方向0630\HANDOFF_交接文件.md`（含转向完整因果链、四次判负、那把"尺子"、CGBC/GBmooer 对照、idea 设计与算法、145 篇精华、第一闸门 kill-test、全部红线、环境资产）
2. ✅ 记忆已更新（新会话能接住转向）

4. ⬜ 新窗口基于结果写**第一份最小验证计划（kill-test）**

新窗口开始时，让它先读 `HANDOFF_交接文件.md`，再读你贴的 deep-research 结果，然后写 kill-test 计划。**特别提醒新窗口：第一步是 kill-test（第4节），不是写完整方法——这是防止第五次"被吸收"的护城河。**

1	# 项目交接文件 · 开放意图识别 + 粒球新方向（HANDOFF）
2	
3	> 写给：新窗口的 Claude（以及未来的我自己）
4	> 写于：2026-06-30，由上一个窗口在 45 天 SoftDist 探索收尾、正式转向时生成
5	> 用途：让新窗口在零上下文的情况下，完整接住"为什么转这个方向、怎么转过来的、粒球领域的精华、当前 idea 的设计与算法、绝不能再踩的坑"。**信息冗余是故意的——宁可多写，不可漏写。**
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 0. 一句话现状
10	
11	经过 45 天（不是一年）、四十多个预注册 Phase 的探索，**"粒球 + 图（GRACE H + GCN）做噪声标签鲁棒分类/检测/聚类" 这条线已被四次干净判负，正式关闭**。现转向新方向：**开放意图识别（open intent / open-set / OOD）中，用粒球做"已知类的多粒度局部边界 + 不确定性几何 + 未知拒识"，并让粒球信号在训练过程中动态参与（课程/置信度调度），而不是静态后处理**。本文件交接这次转向的全部思路、证据、idea 设计与红线。
12	
13	**用户身份**：研究生，课题组是搞粒球计算的（重庆邮电夏书银/王国胤生态是同源主场）。**所有回复必须用中文。** 风格：要结论不要长篇；先 smoke 再多 seed；最小改动；实验必须预注册 go/no-go 闸门 + shuffled 对照 + 多 seed 配对。**用户用 AI（Claude 写计划评估、Codex 在 7700XT ROCm 上跑实验、网页 GPT 做 deep-research）把别人一年的工作量压缩进 45 天——这是关键背景，意味着"快速验证想法"是这个项目的核心打法。**
14	
15	**硬约束**：总时间 **2 个月**（≈8-9 周），减去写作留 **5-6 周实验窗口**。显卡 **7700XT（RDNA3, 16GB, ROCm）**，能跑 BERT-base 微调 / 1D-CNN / ResNet，跑不了大模型。**5-6 周只够做"一个角色 + 一个域 + 一篇论文"，不够两个域都试。**
16	
17	---
18	
19	## 1. 为什么放弃图领域——完整因果链（这是全项目最贵的认知，绝不能丢）
20	
21	### 1.1 起点
22	最初模仿两篇组里的成功论文 **CGBC**（智能合约漏洞检测，TPAMI 投稿）和 **GBmooer / gbMOOER**（文本标签平滑），它们的公式是：**对比学习预训练表示 → 表示空间里建粒球 → 球内多数票/标签分布做软去噪 → 端到端训练分类器**。用户想"换个任务（图节点）套同样公式"，于是做了 **SoftDist[X‖H]**：GRACE 对比预训练 → 冻结 H → H 空间建粒球 → 球内 train 噪声标签投票 → 软标签 → 喂给 GCN[X‖H]。
23	
24	### 1.2 四次判负（按时间，每次都是预注册闸门 + 诚实判负）
25	1. **分类（Phase 24 公平对照）**：给强 baseline NRGNN 同样的 [X‖H] 后，SoftDist 不再领先（Cora 平、CiteSeer/Coauthor-CS 负）。主张从"匹配/超过 NRGNN"降级为"对 CE 和 shuffled 有受控球增量，但**不是 SOTA**"。
26	2. **噪声检测换题（Phase 39）**：球的 LOO 噪声检测分数 `s_ball_loo` 绝对 AUROC 很强（0.83–0.96），**但被 kNN-in-H / GCN-置信度稳定压制**，`corr(ball, kNN-in-H)=0.78–0.90`。结论：**球 = H 空间的粗粒化 kNN。**
27	3. **跨视角矛盾检测（Phase 40）**：试图让球捕捉"原始 X 球 vs H 球的局部多数标签冲突"这种单空间 kNN 看不到的信号。结果**反向**：冲突节点反而更干净（delta −0.03），条件 AUROC 远低于两 kNN 取并。彻底判负。
28	4. **免K粒球图聚类（Phase 41）**：H 上建球→球凝聚成簇，卖点"免K + 误设K鲁棒"。结果 ACC 比"喂真K的 kmeans"低 10–15pp，且 G4 全失败（球凝聚 ≤ "自动定K后 kmeans"，球这步是冗余甚至负贡献）。NO-GO。
29	
30	### 1.3 统一根因——"那把更高维度的尺子"（务必记住，这是判断一切新方向的准绳）
31	> **粒球价值 = max(0, 球提供的结构 − 下游/已有简单方法已能获取的结构)。**
32	
33	四次判负全是同一个病：**球在 GRACE H 上做的"局部一致性/局部统计"，被同一空间里更简单的方法（kNN-in-H / GCN-conf / kmeans）做掉了，甚至做得更好。** 图节点 + 强自监督表示（GRACE H）恰好是"表示已经很好 + 下游 GCN 也吃 H + 图本身有邻接结构先验"三重不利叠加——这是粒球**最不占优**的战场。
34	
35	### 1.4 对照 CGBC/GBmooer 为什么成功（关键差异，决定新方向怎么设计）
36	| | CGBC / GBmooer（成功） | SoftDist（失败） |
37	|---|---|---|
38	| 数据 | 代码/文本，**原始特征/自训练表示** | 图节点，**GRACE 通用对比表示 H** |
39	| 表示与下游 | **同一个端到端网络，球的损失反传塑造编码器** | **冻结 H + 解耦的全新 GCN，球在梯度流外** |
40	| 下游强度 | 弱（编码器本身缺局部结构，球填了洞） | 强（GCN 消息传递天生有局部结构，球冗余） |
41	| 球的位置 | 在训练动力学**里** | 在输出端做**静态后处理** |
42	
43	**两个致命教训**：
44	- **教训A（同源吸收）**：球建在哪个空间、下游就吃哪个空间 → 球必被该空间的简单方法吸收。
45	- **教训B（架构错误）**：145 篇成功论文**没有一篇是"冻结表示 + 离线建球"的单向流水线**，全是端到端耦合。SoftDist 从架构上就偏离了成功范式。
46	
47	---
48	
49	## 2. 为什么转"开放意图 / open-set"——决策逻辑
50	
51	### 2.1 换域候选与淘汰
52	- **故障诊断噪声标签**（MgCNL/MgBIF 已证粒球有效、下游弱）：求稳，但①是新领域要补课（轴承数据/工况协议），2个月内补课吃掉方法时间；②仍是"组内噪声旧范式增量"，易被审稿人说"又一个粒球去噪模块"；③投稿社区陌生。**淘汰为次选。**
53	- **图像带噪标签/长尾**（G-GBC/GBRIP/CIFAR）：数据现成但更卷、球角色不如 open-set 契合。**次选。**
54	- **开放集/开放意图（选中）**：见下。
55	
56	### 2.2 为什么 open-set 是最优（三条硬理由）
57	1. **问题本身需要粒球擅长的东西**——open-set 的核心问题是"这个样本在不在已知类的覆盖区内？该不该拒识？"。**粒球的半径 = 覆盖范围、球间重叠 = 模糊边界、局部密度 = 不确定性**——这些**直接就是答案**，不是把球硬塞进去。这是球第一次从配角变主角。
58	2. **最省时间且最契合 2 个月窗口**——NLP 开放意图（CLINC150 / BANKING77 / StackOverflow）有现成 BERT/Sentence-BERT embedding，编码器几乎不用动，5-6 周能花在方法上而非补课。**注意：这一点和"在 open-set 域用冻结表示+后验粒球边界是合规的"相互成立**——open-set 标准做法本来就是"预训练表示 + post-hoc 拒识打分"（很多 OOD 方法是 post-hoc 的），所以这个域允许"冻结表示+球后验"，不像分类域那样违背范式（这是上一窗口收回"必须端到端"强主张的原因）。
59	3. **组里有起点**——**MOGB**（Multi-granularity Open intent classification via adaptive Granular-Ball decision boundary，组里论文）已把粒球当 open-intent 决策边界用，但**只做到"决策边界"，没做成"多粒度不确定性几何 + 训练动态调度"**。导师认这个方向，且空间没被做透。
60	
61	### 2.3 评测必须换（这是 open-set 让"半径/密度/边界"有发挥空间的前提）
62	**不要只看 accuracy。** 必须用：**AUROC、FPR95（FPR@95%TPR）、unknown-class F1、macro-F1、ECE（校准误差）**，以及"已知类准确率 vs 未知拒识"的权衡曲线。
63	
64	---
65	
66	## 3. 当前 idea 的完整设计与算法（最重要，绝不能漏）

68	### 3.0 idea 的"角色"定义（三方——Claude/Codex/用户——锁定的主线）

21	Open intent classiﬁcation aims to correctly classify the known intents into their corresponding classes while iden-
22	tifying unknown intents. However, most existing methods assume clean training data, overlooking the prevalent 
23	label noise in real-world scenarios, including both in-distribution (IND) and out-of-distribution (OOD) noise. 
24	Moreover, existing noise-handling approaches typically rely on a single-criterion rule for identifying noisy sam-
25	ples, with limited consideration of neighborhood information, and they rarely explore the potential beneﬁts that 
26	noise may oﬀer for representation learning. To address these issues, we propose a Beneﬁcial Noise-guided Open 
27	Intent Classiﬁcation method via Granular-Ball Representation (BNO-GB). Speciﬁcally, we perform unsupervised 
28	granular-ball clustering to obtain noise-resistant granular-ball representations. Based on these representations, 
29	we design two complementary indicators, the Granular-ball-level Outlier Distribution Tendency (G-ODT) and 
30	the Sample-level Inlier Consistency Degree (S-ICD), to build a multi-level noise recognition scheme that sepa-
31	rates clean samples, IND noise, OOD noise, and uncertain cases. Using the identiﬁed noise types, we introduce 
32	a beneﬁcial noise-guided representation learning strategy. Extensive experiments across multiple datasets and 
33	noise conditions demonstrate the eﬀectiveness and robustness of our approach. The source code of BNO-GB is 
34	available at: https://github.com/Liyanhuaa/BNO_GB.
35	1.  Introduction
36	Open intent classiﬁcation [1] aims to enable a model not only to 
37	recognize known intents seen during training but also to detect novel, 
38	unseen intents at inference time, a capability that is essential for practi-
39	cal dialogue systems. However, training data collected from real-world 
40	applications often contains various forms of label noise, making this 
41	task substantially more challenging. The noise typically includes in-
42	distribution (IND) noise, where samples originating from known classes 
43	are mislabeled as other known classes, and out-of-distribution (OOD) 
44	noise, where samples from external distributions are incorrectly anno-
45	tated as known classes [2]. Both noise types disrupt the learning of stable 
46	representations for known intents and hinder the formation of a reliable 
47	boundary for unknown intents. A common line of work in noisy-label 
48	learning adopts a “sample selection followed by representation learn-
49	ing” paradigm [3,4], in which samples are ﬁrst distinguished accord-
50	ing to their noise type and then optimized with diﬀerentiated learning 
51	strategies.
52	Sample selection aims to partition training data into clean samples, 
53	IND noise, and OOD noise by assessing the reliability of each instance

57	renlf@swufe.edu.cn (L. Ren), yangxin@swufe.edu.cn (X. Yang).
58	through speciﬁc criteria. Representative methods typically rely on a sin-
59	gle criterion, such as small-loss selection [3], prediction consistency [5], 
60	or distance to prototypes [6]. While such criteria can work reasonably 
61	well in controlled settings, depending on a single type of evidence makes 
62	the decision process vulnerable to noisy or ambiguous samples. More-

64	mation for noise identiﬁcation, ignoring the valuable cues embedded in 
65	local agreement and distribution deviation.
66	In the area of noisy-label representation learning, numerous strate-
67	gies have been proposed to improve robustness, including reweighted 
68	objectives [7], contrastive regularization [8], and noise-aware feature 
69	correction [9]. Beyond these techniques, an emerging line of research 
70	has highlighted the constructive role of noise. For instance, positive-
71	incentive noise reduces task complexity and facilitates more eﬀective 
72	optimization [10,11]; noise-driven augmentation is now viewed as an 
73	estimator of beneﬁcial noise that strengthens contrastive learning [12]; 
74	and structured beneﬁcial noise embedded into pretrained models sup-
75	ports incremental learning while preserving old-class discrimination 
76	[13]. These ﬁndings collectively reveal that noise can provide meaning-
77	ful learning signals. However, the beneﬁcial nature of noise has not yet

87	been explored in open intent classiﬁcation. Developing eﬀective ways 
88	to transform noisy samples into useful signals for open-world represen-
89	tation learning remains an important but unresolved challenge.
90	For sample selection, we draw inspiration from granular-ball com-
91	puting [14]. Granular-ball clustering [15] adaptively groups nearby 
92	samples into local units and represents the data distribution with a set of 
93	balls, each characterized by attributes such as centroid, radius, purity, 
94	and label. The label of a granular-ball is determined by the majority la-
95	bel of its contained samples, which naturally suppresses the inﬂuence of 
96	noisy labels and thus provides stronger robustness in high-noise scenar-
97	ios. More importantly, the attributes of a granular-ball, together with 
98	its relationships to neighboring balls, reveal many aspects of both the 
99	ball itself and the samples it contains. As illustrated in Fig. 1, which pro-
100	vides an example of the granular-balls derived from clustering, granular-
101	ball A is assigned the label “blue”, but its neighboring balls exhibit in-
102	consistent labels, and it also lies far from other balls sharing the label 
103	“blue”. This large deviation, together with its low purity, suggests that 
104	granular-ball A likely corresponds to a region dominated by OOD noise, 
105	and therefore samples 1-4 inside it have a high probability of being OOD 
106	noise. In contrast, granular-ball B shows high label agreement with its 
107	surrounding balls and exhibits high purity, indicating that it represents 
108	in-distribution samples. Based on the consistency between sample labels 
109	and the label of granular-ball B, sample 5 can be identiﬁed as IND noise, 
110	whereas samples 6–9 can be regarded as clean samples. Thus, granular-
111	ball representation enables the design of multi-perspective indicators for 
112	identifying noise types, which in turn supports more eﬀective represen-
113	tation learning.
114	Building on these observations, we introduce a Beneﬁcial Noise-
115	guided Open Intent Classiﬁcation method via Granular-Ball Represen-
116	tation (BNO-GB). Speciﬁcally, we perform granular-ball clustering in a 
117	label-agnostic and unsupervised manner to obtain granular-ball repre-
118	sentation of the training features, which alleviates the adverse impact 
119	of mislabeled samples. In addition, the granular-ball representation en-
120	ables us to design two complementary indicators from distinct view-
121	points, which collectively constitute a multi-level noise sample selection 
122	strategy. At the granular-ball level, we propose the Granular-ball-level 
123	Outlier Distribution Tendency (G-ODT) to estimate the likelihood that 
124	a granular-ball primarily consists of OOD noise. At the sample level, we 
125	design the Sample-level Inlier Consistency Degree (S-ICD) to measure 
126	how well a sample ﬁts the distribution of its assigned granular-ball. 
127	Combining these two indicators enables us to partition the data into 
128	clean samples, IND noise, OOD noise, and uncertain cases. Based on the 
129	identiﬁed noise types, we further develop a beneﬁcial noise-guided op-
130	timization scheme. The OOD Dispersion Loss allows OOD noise to act as 
131	a constructive signal for shaping the open region by encouraging sep-
132	aration between known intents and the potential unknown space. The 
133	Prototype Softmax Loss and the Prototype Margin Loss encourage clean 
134	and corrected IND samples to acquire more discriminative, class-speciﬁc 
135	representations. These objectives are jointly optimized to promote ro-
136	bust representation learning. Overall, the contributions of this work are 
137	as follows:
138	(1) We propose BNO-GB, a new framework for open intent classiﬁ-
139	cation under noisy conditions, which introduces a novel noise identiﬁ-
140	cation mechanism and a beneﬁcial noise-guided optimization strategy 
141	based on granular-ball representation.
142	(2) Building on granular-ball representation, we design two com-
143	plementary indicators that capture deviation at the ball level and con-
144	sistency at the sample level, thereby constructing a multi-level noise 
145	sample selection strategy. Based on the identiﬁed noise types, we fur-
146	ther develop a beneﬁcial noise-guided optimization scheme that jointly 
147	leverages OOD Dispersion Loss, Prototype Softmax Loss, and Prototype 
148	Margin Loss to enhance representation learning.
149	(3) We conduct extensive experiments across multiple datasets and 
150	noise conﬁgurations, demonstrating clear improvements over represen-
151	tative baselines in noise identiﬁcation and open intent classiﬁcation. The 
152	results verify the eﬀectiveness and generality of the proposed approach.
153	2.  Related work
154	2.1.  Learning with noisy labels
155	Learning with noisy labels is fundamental in robust deep learning. 
156	Existing studies can be grouped into four major categories. Sample se-
157	lection methods [16,17], which identify diﬀerent noise types based on 
158	heuristics such as small-loss criterion or consistency across views, and 
159	use this information to guide robust training. These methods exhibit 
160	complementary strengths under diﬀerent noise conditions. Label correc-
161	tion methods [18,19], which attempt to directly revise incorrect labels, 
162	either via model predictions or auxiliary estimation strategies. Loss cor-
163	rection methods [20,21], which design robust objective functions that 
164	are less sensitive to noisy annotations and stabilize the optimization pro-
165	cess. Transition matrix-based methods [22,23], which aim to explicitly 
166	model the noise generation process by estimating the label transition 
167	probabilities and correcting posterior predictions accordingly.
168	Recent studies highlight the importance of handling both IND noise 
169	and OOD noise in open-world scenarios. Xia et al. [24] design an ex-
170	tended 𝑇-estimator to model mixed noise through a cluster-dependent 
171	transition matrix. Zhang et al. [6] propose a multi-prototype framework 
172	that separates diﬀerent types of noisy samples via prototype-sample dis-
173	tances. In addition, recent work shows that controlled noise can ben-
174	eﬁt diverse modalities. For instance, incentive noise improves vision-
175	language alignment [25], learned graph noise enhances contrastive 
176	augmentation [26], frequency-guided variation beneﬁts image gener-
177	ation [27], initialization-based modulation preserves pretrained knowl-
178	edge in diﬀusion transformers [28], and facial adversarial noise supports 
179	privacy-preserving portrait synthesis [29].
180	Despite recent progress, most existing noise detection methods rely 
181	on single-aspect cues for noise identiﬁcation and seldom incorporate 
182	neighborhood information, which limits their ability to distinguish IND 
183	and OOD noise. In this work, we propose to identify noisy samples by 
184	constructing multi-perspective indicators and treat OOD noise as a ben-
185	eﬁcial signal to improve representation.
186	2.2.  Open intent classiﬁcation
187	Open Intent Classiﬁcation [30,31] aims to classify intents belonging 
188	to predeﬁned intent classes while detecting open (unknown) intents. 
189	This setting is critical in real-world dialogue systems, where new user 
190	intents frequently emerge. Compared with closed-set classiﬁcation, it 
191	requires both discriminative modeling of known intents and robust de-
192	tection of unknowns.
193	Existing open intent classiﬁcation approaches can be broadly 
194	grouped into two categories. The ﬁrst is post-hoc unknown detec-
195	tion, which builds OOD detection mechanisms upon pretrained or 
196	Pattern Recognition 177 (2026) 113283 
197	2 
198	
199	Y. Li et al.
200	ﬁne-tuned representations. This includes (1) classiﬁer-based methods 
201	that compute conﬁdence scores from output logits, such as OLT [32], 
202	which calibrates sparse subnetworks for improved detection; and (2) 
203	distance-based methods, such as using learned class-wise radii to detect
204	unknowns [1]. The second is learning discriminative representations for 
205	OOD detection, which aims to optimize the feature space to separate 
206	known and unknown intents. For instance, DeepUnk [33] introduces a 
207	margin loss to enlarge inter-class gaps and reduce intra-class variance. 
208	Additionally, some methods utilize pseudo-OOD samples to guide repre-
209	sentation learning; for example, K+1-way [34] constructs pseudo out-
210	liers to train a discriminative classiﬁer.
211	Despite recent progress, most methods assume clean training data 
212	and overlook label noise, which is common in large-scale intent datasets. 
213	Although a few works in computer vision have explored open-node 
214	recognition under label noise [2], they remain limited to the image 
215	domain. Existing studies have rarely addressed the coexistence of IND 
216	and OOD noise in open intent classiﬁcation. This work ﬁlls the gap by 
217	proposing a uniﬁed framework that identiﬁes multiple noise types and 
218	exploits OOD noise to improve open-space representation learning.
219	2.3.  Granular-ball computing
220	Granular-ball computing was ﬁrst practically implemented by Xia et 
221	al. [14] as an eﬃcient and interpretable method for multi-granularity 
222	data representation. Unlike traditional point-based data, it employs 
223	spherical structures of varying sizes to adaptively partition and cover the 
224	data space, thereby improving expressive capacity, eﬃciency, and ro-
225	bustness when handling complex data. This paradigm has been applied 
226	in various domains, including granular-ball clustering [15], granular-
227	ball classiﬁcation [35], granular-ball sampling [36], and others.
228	Owing to its coarse-grained and robust representations, granular-ball 
229	computing has recently been explored for addressing noise-related chal-
230	lenges. For example, Wang et al. [37] applied granular-ball mechanisms 
231	to adversarial text defense, mitigating the impact of input perturbations. 
232	Wang et al. [38] utilized granular-balls to ﬁlter noisy labels and enhance 
233	model generalization.
234	While these studies demonstrate the potential of granular-ball com-
235	puting under noisy conditions, they mostly rely on basic granular-ball 
236	properties for coarse ﬁltering and focus solely on IND noise. In contrast, 
237	we propose to design multi-perspective indicators based on granular-
238	ball representations for identifying both IND and OOD noise, aiming to 
239	enhance open intent classiﬁcation under noisy scenarios.
240	3.  Preliminaries
241	3.1.  Granular-ball
242	Following the general formulation of granular-ball computing [36], 
243	we introduce the basic concepts used in this work. Let 𝑍= {(𝑧𝑖, 𝑦𝑖) ∣𝑖=
244	1, 2, … , 𝑁} denote a set of representations, where 𝑧𝑖 is a feature vector 
245	and 𝑦𝑖 is its associated class label. Based on 𝑍, a set of granular-balls is 
246	constructed and denoted as 𝐺= { 𝑔𝑏𝑗∣𝑗= 1, 2, … , 𝑚}, where 𝑔𝑏𝑗 repre-
247	sents the 𝑗th granular-ball. Each granular-ball 𝑔𝑏𝑗 contains a subset of 
248	samples, formally written as 𝑔𝑏𝑗= {(𝑧𝑗,𝑘, 𝑦𝑗,𝑘) ∣𝑘= 1, 2, … , 𝑛𝑗}, where 𝑛𝑗
249	denotes the size of the granular-ball, i.e., the number of samples it con-
250	tains. The centroid 𝑜𝑗 of a granular-ball 𝑔𝑏𝑗 is calculated as the mean 
251	of all feature vectors it contains. The radius of 𝑔𝑏𝑗 is deﬁned in two 
252	ways: the maximum radius 𝑟𝑗, which denotes the largest Euclidean dis-
253	tance from any sample to the centroid, and the mean radius 𝔯𝑗, which 
254	denotes the average Euclidean distance from each sample to the cen-
255	troid. For granular-ball 𝑔𝑏𝑗, its label set 𝐿𝑗 is deﬁned as the collec-
256	tion of class labels corresponding to the samples within the ball, i.e., 
257	𝐿𝑗= {𝑦𝑗,𝑘∣(𝑧𝑗,𝑘, 𝑦𝑗,𝑘) ∈𝑔𝑏𝑗}. The label 𝑙𝑗 assigned to 𝑔𝑏𝑗 is determined 
258	by the most frequent label in 𝐿𝑗. The purity 𝑝𝑗 of a granular-ball is then

260	reﬂecting the degree of label consistency within the ball.

267	class is denoted as the (𝐶+1)th class, i.e., 𝐼Unknown = {(𝐶+1)}, which is

289	4.  Methodology
290	As shown in Fig. 2, the proposed BNO-GB framework consists of three 
291	main modules. First, we perform unsupervised granular-ball clustering 
292	over the extracted features to approximate the underlying data distribu-
293	tion with adaptive and noise-tolerant local structures. Then, we design 
294	a multi-level noise identiﬁcation strategy by combining two comple-
295	mentary indicators: a global granular-ball-level indicator to assess the 
296	outlier tendency (G-ODT), and a local sample-level indicator to evaluate 
297	inlier consistency (S-ICD). Based on these indicators, samples are cate-
298	gorized into clean, IND noise, OOD noise, and uncertain types. Finally, 
299	we introduce a beneﬁcial noise-guided representation learning module, 
300	where three tailored losses are applied to guide OOD samples away from 
301	known-class prototypes, aggregate clean and corrected IND samples to-
302	ward their prototypes, and enforce margins between class prototypes 
303	to enhance discrimination. In inference, we use multi-granularity de-
304	cision boundaries for each class to classify known classes and identify 
305	unknown.
306	4.1.  Granular-ball-based space approximation
307	Discovering the neighborhood information and the latent class struc-
308	ture from noisy data is essential for reliable noise identiﬁcation. Prior 
309	works have adopted clustering-based approaches to estimate multiple 
310	prototypes per class to assist in detecting label noise [6]. However, these 
311	methods typically require a predeﬁned number of clusters for each class 
312	and often rely on supervised clustering guided by noisy labels, which 
313	can degrade clustering performance. To address this issue, we propose 
314	to approximate the underlying representation space using unsupervised 
315	granular-ball clustering [15], which avoids reliance on noisy labels and 
316	adaptively ﬁts the data distribution. Compared with conventional clus-
317	tering methods, granular-ball clustering captures local density, region 
318	coverage, and structural continuity, making it more eﬀective in reﬂect-
319	ing the spatial structure of data. The resulting properties of granular-ball 
320	provide more depictions of data distribution, oﬀering a stronger foun-
321	dation for downstream noise detection.
322	Given a dataset 𝐷, we feed the input samples into a pre-trained BERT 
323	model [39] to extract feature representations 𝑍= {(𝑧𝑖, 𝑦𝑖)}𝑁
324	𝑖=1. These 
325	representations are then clustered in an unsupervised manner to form a 
326	set of granular-balls. The granular-ball clustering process consists of two 
327	stages: ball generation and ball merging. The overall process is detailed 
328	as follows.

674	To fully integrate the advantages of the above three component 
675	losses, we formulate a uniﬁed objective function as follows:
676	𝑡𝑜𝑡𝑎𝑙= 𝛼⋅𝑑𝑖𝑠𝑝+ 𝛽⋅𝑝𝑟𝑜𝑡𝑜+ 𝛾⋅𝑚𝑎𝑟𝑔𝑖𝑛,
677	(16)
678	where 𝛼, 𝛽, and 𝛾 are hyperparameters that control the relative impor-
679	tance of each loss component. These three mechanisms work collabo-
680	ratively to construct a more compact and discriminative feature space, 
681	signiﬁcantly boosting the model’s generalization ability and unknown 
682	intent recognition performance in open-world scenarios.
683	4.4.  Inference strategy
684	 To perform open intent classiﬁcation during inference, we adopt a 
685	multi-granularity classiﬁer that builds upon the granular-ball structures 
686	constructed in the representation space [40]. For each known class, we 
687	retain its granular-balls with high purity and size (𝑝> 𝑝𝑡, 𝑛> 𝑛𝑡) to rep-
688	resent its class region, each deﬁned by a centroid and a corresponding 
689	mean radius. These granular-balls serve as ﬂexible decision regions that 
690	reﬂect the intrinsic distribution of each class. Given a query representa-
691	tion, we determine whether it belongs to any known class by checking 
692	its distance relative to the centroids of all retained granular-balls. If the 
693	query falls outside the radius of every granular-ball, it is considered an 
694	unknown sample and assigned to the unknown class. Otherwise, it is 
695	classiﬁed into the class of the closest granular-ball that covers it. This 
696	localized, prototype-based decision strategy enables the model to more 
697	accurately distinguish known intents while eﬀectively rejecting open-
698	space unknowns.
699	4.5.  Time complexity analysis
700	The granular-ball generation module in BNO-GB follows the splitting 
701	and merging strategy used in MGNR [15]. During the splitting stage, 
702	each granular-ball is recursively divided until the purity and size con-
703	straints are satisﬁed. The most time-consuming operation is the iterative 
704	determination of ball centers by repeatedly identifying farthest points, 
705	which requires 𝑂(𝑁) time per iteration. Since the maximum number of 
706	iterations is log 𝑁, the overall time complexity of the splitting stage is 
707	𝑂(𝑁log 𝑁). In the merging stage, the algorithm evaluates pairwise simi-
708	larities among the generated granular-balls and performs iterative merg-
709	ing operations. Let 𝑀 denote the number of granular-balls after split-
710	ting, typically with 𝑀≪𝑁; consequently, the merging process takes 
711	𝑂(𝑀log 𝑀) time.
712	5.  Experiments
713	In this section, we empirically investigate the open intent classiﬁca-
714	tion performance of our proposed BNO-GB method in dealing with IND 
715	noise and OOD noise. In the following, we describe the experimental set-
716	tings (Section 5.1), experimental results (Section 5.2), ablation studies 
717	(Section 5.3), analysis of the G-ODT and S-ICD indicators (Section 5.4), 
718	impact of key parameters during inference (Section 5.5), and computa-
719	tional cost analysis (Section 5.6).
720	5.1.  Experimental setup
721	5.1.1.  Datasets
722	To comprehensively assess the eﬀectiveness of BNO-GB across di-
723	verse intent classiﬁcation scenarios, we experiment on three repre-
724	sentative text datasets commonly used in open intent classiﬁcation.
725	SNIPS [41] is a lightweight dataset for voice assistant intent recog-
726	nition, containing 7 intent classes with concise user queries. Stack-
727	Overﬂow [42] is a multi-domain dataset with 20 technical intent 
728	classes, drawn from developer Q&A posts with diverse linguistic pat-
729	terns. BANKING [43] is a domain-speciﬁc dataset covering 77 banking-
730	related intent classes, featuring ﬁne-grained and formal customer ser-
731	vice queries. An overview of the datasets is given below, with detailed 
732	statistics summarized in Table 1. For each dataset, we introduce con-
733	trolled noise to simulate real-world challenges, with details of the noise 
734	setting shown in (Section 5.1.2).
735	5.1.2.  Open and noise setting

737	domly selecting a ﬁxed proportion of classes as known classes for train-
738	ing. The remaining classes of the dataset are treated as unknown classes 
739	and are used only during testing. The training set contains clean samples, 
740	IND noise, and OOD noise. All training samples are assigned labels ex-
741	clusively from the known class set. Speciﬁcally, IND noise is introduced 
742	by corrupting a portion of known-class samples through random misla-
743	beling within the known classes. OOD noise is generated by sampling

787	5.1.3.  Comparison methods
788	To evaluate the performance of BNO-GB, we compare it with three 
789	categories of baseline methods. The ﬁrst category includes open intent 
790	classiﬁcation methods, which aim to detect unknown intents while ac-
791	curately classifying known ones. Speciﬁcally, we compare with Deep-
792	Unk (2019) [33], K+1-way (2021) [34], DETER (2024) [44], and OLT
793	(2024) [32]. The second category is granular-ball-based noise-robust 
794	classiﬁcation methods. We adopt GBRAIN (2024) [38] as a represen-
795	tative baseline. Since it lacks the ability to detect unknown intents, 
796	we incorporate an adaptive decision boundary [1] to enable open in-
797	tent identiﬁcation. The third category includes Large Language Model 
798	(LLM) baselines, where we adopt Qwen2-7B-Instruct and Baichuan2-
799	7B-Chat for open intent classiﬁcation. All methods are evaluated using 
800	four metrics consistent with prior work [33], including overall Accu-
801	racy (Acc), macro F1-score across all classes (F1-All), macro F1-score 
802	over known classes (Known), and macro F1-score over the open class 
803	(Open). These metrics oﬀer a comprehensive assessment of both gen-
804	eral and ﬁne-grained performance.
805	5.1.4.  Implementation details
806	We use a pre-trained BERT model [39], where all parameters are 
807	frozen except for the ﬁnal classiﬁcation layer. Training is conducted 
808	with a batch size of 128 and an initial learning rate of 2e-5. The train-
809	ing process consists of 10 warm-up epochs, followed by noise recogni-
810	tion and beneﬁcial noise learning. The total number of training epochs 
811	is set to 100, with early stopping applied using a patience of 10. Dur-
812	ing granular-ball clustering, only granular-balls with sample size greater 
813	than a threshold 𝑛𝑠𝑝𝑙𝑖𝑡 are split. Based on dataset scale, 𝑛𝑠𝑝𝑙𝑖𝑡 is set to 16 
814	for StackOverﬂow and BANKING, and 150 for SNIPS. In the multi-level 
815	noise identiﬁcation module, the number of neighbors for the G-ODT in-
816	dicator is set to 𝑀= 5, and the consistency neighbor size for G-IND is 
817	𝑇= 5. To select reliable prototypes, we use centroids of granular-balls 
818	with purity 𝑝ℎ> 0.7 and sample size 𝑛ℎ> 5 across all datasets. For noise 
819	type classiﬁcation (Eq. (8)), the threshold 𝜃𝑔 is uniformly set to 0.1, 
820	while 𝜃𝑠 is set to 0.25 for BANKING and StackOverﬂow, and 0.35 for 
821	SNIPS. In the beneﬁcial noise learning stage, three loss functions are 
822	jointly optimized: OOD Dispersion Loss 𝑑𝑖𝑠𝑝 (Eq. (9)) with 𝑀𝑜= 5 and 
823	𝜏= 6.0; Prototype Softmax Loss 𝑝𝑟𝑜𝑡𝑜 (Eq. 12); and Prototype Margin 
824	Loss 𝑚𝑎𝑟𝑔𝑖𝑛 (Eq. (14)) with margin 𝛿= 0.5. The weights of these losses 
825	are set to 𝛼= 1.0, 𝛽= 1.0, and 𝛾= 1.0, respectively.
826	During inference, decision boundaries are constructed using the cen-
827	troids and radii of granular-balls with purity above 𝑝𝑡 and sample size 
828	above 𝑛𝑡. Speciﬁcally, we set 𝑝𝑡= 0.9 when the training noise ratio is 
829	0.2, and 𝑝𝑡= 0.8 when the noise ratio is 0.4. The value of 𝑛𝑡 is dataset-
830	dependent.
831	5.2.  Experimental results
832	5.2.1.  Main results
833	Table 2 presents the F1-score and Acc of BNO-GB and other base-
834	lines on the SNIPS, StackOverﬂow, and BANKING datasets. Each value 
835	represents the average performance over four runs with diﬀerent ran-
836	dom seeds. The experiments are conducted under two known-class ratios 
837	(25% and 50%) and two noise levels (20% and 40%). The best results 
838	among all methods are highlighted in bold, while the second-best re-
839	sults are marked with underline. From Table 2, we observe that when 
840	the noise level increases from 20% to 40%, both the F1-score and Acc 
841	of BNO-GB decrease on almost all datasets and settings. This is because 
842	a higher noise ratio makes it more challenging to accurately identify 
843	noisy samples and to learn stable intent representations. Table 3 presents 
844	ﬁne-grained F1-scores for known and open classes across the SNIPS, 
845	StackOverﬂow, and BANKING datasets under diﬀerent combinations of 
846	known-class ratios (25% and 50%) and noise levels (20% and 40%). 
847	From Table 3, we observe that for BNO-GB, increasing the known-class 
848	ratio from 25% to 50% generally leads to higher F1-scores on known 
849	classes but lower F1-scores on open classes. This phenomenon can be 
850	explained by the fact that a larger known-class ratio provides richer su-
851	pervision and clearer intra-class structure for distinguishing known in-
852	tents, which improves the F1-score on known classes. However, it also 
853	reduces the relative size of the open space, causing unseen intents to 
854	overlap more with known regions and making open-class detection more 
855	diﬃcult, which leads to lower F1-scores on open classes.
856	By jointly examining Tables 2 and 3, we can see that BNO-GB 
857	achieves the best or highly competitive performance across diﬀerent 
858	datasets, noise ratios, and known-class ratios, and outperforms all base-
859	line methods. These improvements mainly stem from two key compo-
860	nents of our framework. First, the granular-ball-based multi-level noise 
861	identiﬁcation enables more reliable separation of clean samples, IND 
862	noise, and OOD noise, which allows the model to learn from structurally 
863	trustworthy samples even in the presence of severe label noise. Second, 
864	the beneﬁcial noise-guided learning scheme explicitly leverages OOD 
865	noise to shape the open region and reinforces the separation between 
866	known and unknown intents. The combination of these two components 
867	leads to more discriminative representations and more accurate open in-
868	tent detection.
869	In addition, we observe that the LLM-based Qwen2-7B-Instruct 
870	achieves relatively good performance on the SNIPS and StackOverﬂow 
871	datasets, where several metrics reach the second-best level. However, 
872	its performance degrades signiﬁcantly on the BANKING dataset, which 
873	suggests that current large models still face challenges when dealing 
874	with tasks involving a larger number of intent categories. We also ﬁnd 
875	that Baichuan2-7B-Chat performs much worse than Qwen2-7B-Instruct 
876	under almost all settings. Overall, BNO-GB surpasses both LLM-based 
877	baselines, which further demonstrates the eﬀectiveness and robustness 
878	of the proposed method.
